newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet slumps for third day in row.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet slumps for third day in row.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel prices fell sharply for the third-day in a row on market perception that winter demand has ended as physical offers emerged at low levels, traders said on Wednesday.
Jet fuel prices have lost more than $2.00 per barrel since the start of this week initially on strong selling in the swaps market and on Wednesday in the physical market.
A trader offered 100,000-barrels at $28.50 per barrel for Mar 10-14 lifting, sharply lower than Tuesday's buying price of $30.10 a barrel for Feb 26-Mar 2 lifting fob for 100,000 barrels.
The weaker market was also reflected in Taiwan's monthly jet fuel buy tender which was awarded on Thursday at $234 per tonne for March delivery, down from the $261 paid for February cargoes.
In the swaps market, the February regrade (jet fuel/gas oil swaps spread) was last quoted at $2.50/2.90 per barrel against Wednesday's $3.00/$3.40.
Traders said the Singapore gas oil market is holding its own on regional demand despite sharply lower overnight crude prices where March Brent crude lost 62 cents on the IPE.
Unexpected buying was seen from Thailand where refinery problems had forced refiners there to import two 30,000-tonne cargoes from Singapore for February arrival.
Traders said buyers there are still in the market for more cargoes to build up very low stocks.
They are also optimistic on signs of fresh demand from China after the Lunar New year holidays and recent exports of about 80,000-tonnes to India and Bangladesh.
In the local physical market, two offers were heard at an unchanged $25.30 per barrel from Wednesday despite the crude slump in a clear reflection of the renewed buying interest.
Gas oil swaps opened the day to trade at a low of $24.95 per barrel but by late afternoon recovered to trade at $25.20.
